jobs.description:
Scribd, Inc. is on a mission to advance human understanding. Our four products — Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable — help billions of people across the globe move beyond access and into insight, application, and expertise.

Culture at Scribd, Inc.

We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

The Team

Data & Analytics is building the DNA of an AI native Scribd, Inc. Bringing together Analytics Engineering, Data Science, and Data Analytics, D&A partners across product, technology, content, and the business to scale intelligence, advance understanding, shape strategy, and turn insight into lasting growth across our four brand portfolio.

Making this ambition real at scale starts with Analytics Engineering. The team transforms fragmented data, inconsistent definitions, and dispersed analytical knowledge into trusted, reusable, production quality data foundations and products that enable intelligence to scale across the company.

In partnership with Engineering, Analytics Engineers ensure critical data is captured, centralized, documented, secured, and governed. The team builds canonical datasets, shared metrics, and semantic layers, together with the quality, observability, lineage, and evaluation systems that make these assets trustworthy. On top of this foundation, Analytics Engineers develop AI agents and analytical tools that bring reliable intelligence directly into the decisions and workflows of teams across the company.

The Role

We’re hiring for a Director, Analytics Engineering to own scaling data for an AI native Scribd, Inc. You will build, scale, and lead a high performing Analytics Engineering team, turning strong individual contributors into a cohesive and highly effective team. This requires more than hiring and developing exceptional talent. It means establishing an operating model that creates structure without unnecessary bureaucracy, fostering culture and community that balances local priorities with the broader success of the company, and creating the technical foundations and standards of excellence that enable everyone to do their best work.

Your leadership philosophy is grounded in service. A leader’s role is to provide clarity, create context, remove obstacles, and help others succeed. You will strengthen team dynamics, ensure great work is recognized, create meaningful career pathways, and help individuals navigate obstacles and opportunities throughout their careers. Durable teams are built by distributing ownership, developing leaders, and creating an environment where people feel trusted, supported, and accountable.

Your pragmatic approach keeps the organization moving forward. Rather than waiting for an ideal end state, you will think in sequences and ask, “What is the right next version?” Communication happens early and often because transparency, thoughtful feedback, and visible decision making build trust and help teams move with confidence.

Your strong strategic judgment is paired with enough proximity to the work to guide technical decisions credibly. You will connect analytics engineering investments to company priorities, communicate tradeoffs clearly to senior leaders, and contribute thoughtfully to decisions about data modeling, architecture, governance, quality, tooling, and developer experience.

The transformation happening through AI is an opportunity to expand what talented teams can accomplish. Agentic coding, AI assisted development and analysis, and automated workflows can increase human judgment, creativity, and impact rather than replace them. You approach these technologies with curiosity and pragmatism, applying them where they create clear and measurable value.

Above all, leadership is about building people and strengthening the discipline they share. Success is reflected in a team that grows more capable, confident, connected, and effective because of your leadership.

The Essentials

10+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, business intelligence engineering or a related discipline, including 5+ years leading and developing technical teams
Proven track record of building, scaling, and leading high performing teams, turning strong individual contributors into cohesive and highly effective teams that are valued as strategic partners
Depth in building governed, canonical data models and semantic layers, giving core business concepts one authoritative, discoverable definition instead of letting teams reconcile competing sources
Experience designing the data quality, observability, documentation, governance, access control, privacy, lineage, and evaluation systems that ensure data and AI products are reliable, explainable, trustworthy, and safe to operate at scale
Advanced SQL skills and production experience with modern data stack, including AWS, Databricks, Airbyte, Fivetran, Looker, or comparable platforms
Demonstrated ability to lead cross functional data initiatives from strategy through production adoption and measurable business impact
Strong judgment in balancing immediate stakeholder needs with long term investments in reusable data products, platform health, and technical debt reduction
Excellent written and verbal communication with technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior executives

The Nice to Haves

Advanced Python
Experience leading data cleanup efforts and implementing role based access controls and data retention policies to improve data quality, security, and governance
Experience designing and building canonical data models and semantic layers that support financial analysis at scale
Experience leading on call rotations, coordinating incident response, resolving production issues, and driving follow up improvements that strengthen system reliability

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell AI Fabric is building Canada's largest sovereign AI infrastructure platform. As Director, Strategy, you will work at the centre of its most important strategic, commercial, and operational priorities, helping shape decisions that will influence the future of AI infrastructure in Canada and ensuring those decisions translate into action and results.

This is a highly visible internal consulting and execution role with unusual breadth and access. Working directly with senior executives, Bell AI Fabric Board members, governments, customers, investors, and strategic partners, you will tackle complex questions with no obvious answer, bring clarity to competing perspectives, and help move the organization from discussion to decision to delivery.

Your work will span corporate strategy, partnerships, government engagement, commercial negotiations, major customer opportunities, and organizational execution. You will build the plans and governance required to deliver, step into critical moments where additional leadership or problem-solving is needed and see recommendations through to real-world outcomes.

This is a unique opportunity for a strategy or consulting professional who wants to help build something consequential, learn quickly across a wide range of issues, and have visible impact. You do not need to arrive knowing every part of the business; success will come from curiosity, sound judgment, strong execution, and a willingness to invest the effort required to figure things out.

Key Responsibilities

Act as a trusted strategy partner and extension of the executive team, bringing independent judgment, anticipating what is required, and providing hands-on leadership on Bell AI Fabric's highest-priority opportunities and issues.
Lead structured problem-solving on complex questions related to growth, market positioning, commercial models, partnerships, major initiatives, and organizational scalability; distill complexity into clear choices, decisions, and actions.
Rapidly develop command of unfamiliar commercial, technical, operational, and stakeholder issues by identifying the critical facts, connecting perspectives, and isolating what matters most.
Develop decision-oriented recommendations and materials for senior executives and the Bell AI Fabric Board, presenting clear options, trade-offs, risks, and proposed actions with accuracy and a compelling narrative.
Evaluate and advance strategic partnerships, commercial opportunities, government initiatives, customer opportunities, and other priorities that support long-term growth.
Translate strategy into executable workplans with clear outcomes, interdependencies, milestones, owners, decision points, and escalation paths.
Drive large, complex, cross-functional projects from initial framing through decision, implementation, and closure; govern progress, remove obstacles, and maintain momentum until the work is complete.
Identify and fix gaps in processes, decision rights, governance, and operating cadence to improve execution, accountability, transparency, and organizational effectiveness.

Critical Qualifications

Typically 8-12 years of experience in management consulting, corporate strategy, infrastructure strategy, corporate development, transactions, or another environment that develops comparable strategic and execution capabilities.
Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems, understand complex issues quickly, separate signal from noise, and translate insights into practical recommendations and action.
Strong PowerPoint, executive communication, and presentation skills, with the ability to develop precise and persuasive materials for senior executives and the Bell AI Fabric Board.
Experience building and driving workplans for large, complex, cross-functional initiatives, with disciplined governance, active issue resolution, and ownership through final delivery.
A strong orientation toward quality and detail, with the ability to reconcile analyses, narratives, decisions, and deliverables across multiple workstreams.
Sound commercial judgment and negotiation capability, with the persistence to help close agreements, decisions, and outstanding projects.
Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to govern, align, and mobilize senior stakeholders without formal authority.
High capacity and strong organization, with the ability to manage several urgent priorities, sustain pace, and improve the completeness and quality of the work.
Ability to operate with increasing independence, anticipate needs, step into unfamiliar issues, and invest the effort required to build understanding and deliver results.

Preferred Qualifications

Management consulting experience or equivalent training in structured problem-solving, analysis, executive communication, and high-quality delivery.
Strong research and synthesis capability, intellectual curiosity, and a demonstrated interest in learning and becoming credible on new topics.
Experience supporting partnerships, complex commercial negotiations, or major infrastructure and technology initiatives.
Comfort operating with ambiguity and making clear recommendations when information is incomplete.
Consistently high standards for quality, accuracy, pace, ownership, accountability, and follow-through.
A practical, low-ego working style and willingness to step into priorities where additional leadership, capacity, or problem-solving is required.
Ambition to learn and grow, resilience under pressure, discretion, and a strong bias toward action and completed outcomes.

Adequate knowledge of French is required for positions in Quebec.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Security & IT
jobs.description:
At
Klue
, We’re Building the Future of Competitive Intelligence

We’re looking for a Security, Compliance & IT Leader 👋

As our Director, Enterprise Security & IT
, you'll sit at the intersection of security, compliance, and IT operations. You'll be accountable for how Klue protects customer data and how every Kluebee gets equipped to do their best work. Today, these three areas sit under different teams. You'll turn them into one team with one roadmap, working alongside an Engineering org that already builds and runs our product infrastructure.

Your Mission?
To own the security and compliance posture that our customers, our sales team, and our own people rely on. That covers everything we do: from building the product, to the internal automations, to the tools we use, and how we use AI. You'll set the standard, build the systems and set the rhythm to meet it. And in the process, make the secure way, the easy way.

What's In It for You?

You won't inherit a playbook. You'll write it. You'll define the operating model, the culture, and the technical direction for a brand-new function, and shape a small, sharp team of 2 from day one. You'll report directly to the CTO and work closely with the Senior Leadership Team, as well as the Engineering, Product, Sales, and People teams. You'll tackle big questions like how to govern AI agents connected to company systems, and your answers will set policy at Klue. As Klue grows, so do the team and your scope. You have the power to shape what that looks like.

What You'll Do

Own security posture and incident readiness. Mature how Klue prevents, detects, and responds to security issues. Design the incident response process and governance, and make sure everyone knows their role before something goes wrong.
Run the compliance engine. Own the annual audit cycle against SOC 2 Type II, NIST CSF, and BSIMM, plus penetration testing, from evidence collection to a successful finish. Build audit methodology and documentation that make reviews faster and less painful for the whole company.
Be the security answer for go-to-market. Keep customer questionnaires, external assessments, and audits moving on time. Review and negotiate data protection agreements and security exhibits with customers and vendors so what we sign matches what we do.
Govern vendors, data, and privacy. Run full-spectrum vendor reviews, including sub-processor qualification. Own DLP, data retention, and the privacy framework for an international customer base, including data subject access requests.
Set the rules for AI and high-risk access. Own AI security governance: policies, risk acceptance, data handling, and permissioning for AI tools, agents, and integrations connected to company systems. Define and enforce access governance for high-risk systems, including admin access reviews, service accounts vs. individual credentials, and controls on sensitive logs and data.
Make security engineering's job easier. Set the security and compliance standard for Engineering's security work. Give the team the tooling, policy, and guidelines to build against, and translate their technical work into terms leadership and customers can act on.
Equip and enable every Kluebee. Own devices, access, and tooling across the full employee lifecycle. Manage the vendors behind our IT stack, set and hit reliability targets (SLOs) for corporate systems, and replace ad hoc fixes with repeatable processes that scale. Partner with People so onboarding and offboarding run smoothly. (Product infrastructure stays with Engineering.)

What Success Looks Like

new_jobs.description:
Scribd, Inc. is on a mission to advance human understanding. Our four products — Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable — help billions of people across the globe move beyond access and into insight, application, and expertise.

Culture at Scribd, Inc.

We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

The Team

Data & Analytics is building the DNA of an AI native Scribd, Inc. Bringing together Analytics Engineering, Data Science, and Data Analytics, D&A partners across product, technology, content, and the business to scale intelligence, advance understanding, shape strategy, and turn insight into lasting growth across our four brand portfolio.

Making this ambition real at scale starts with Analytics Engineering. The team transforms fragmented data, inconsistent definitions, and dispersed analytical knowledge into trusted, reusable, production quality data foundations and products that enable intelligence to scale across the company.

In partnership with Engineering, Analytics Engineers ensure critical data is captured, centralized, documented, secured, and governed. The team builds canonical datasets, shared metrics, and semantic layers, together with the quality, observability, lineage, and evaluation systems that make these assets trustworthy. On top of this foundation, Analytics Engineers develop AI agents and analytical tools that bring reliable intelligence directly into the decisions and workflows of teams across the company.

The Role

We’re hiring for a Director, Analytics Engineering to own scaling data for an AI native Scribd, Inc. You will build, scale, and lead a high performing Analytics Engineering team, turning strong individual contributors into a cohesive and highly effective team. This requires more than hiring and developing exceptional talent. It means establishing an operating model that creates structure without unnecessary bureaucracy, fostering culture and community that balances local priorities with the broader success of the company, and creating the technical foundations and standards of excellence that enable everyone to do their best work.

Your leadership philosophy is grounded in service. A leader’s role is to provide clarity, create context, remove obstacles, and help others succeed. You will strengthen team dynamics, ensure great work is recognized, create meaningful career pathways, and help individuals navigate obstacles and opportunities throughout their careers. Durable teams are built by distributing ownership, developing leaders, and creating an environment where people feel trusted, supported, and accountable.

Your pragmatic approach keeps the organization moving forward. Rather than waiting for an ideal end state, you will think in sequences and ask, “What is the right next version?” Communication happens early and often because transparency, thoughtful feedback, and visible decision making build trust and help teams move with confidence.

Your strong strategic judgment is paired with enough proximity to the work to guide technical decisions credibly. You will connect analytics engineering investments to company priorities, communicate tradeoffs clearly to senior leaders, and contribute thoughtfully to decisions about data modeling, architecture, governance, quality, tooling, and developer experience.

The transformation happening through AI is an opportunity to expand what talented teams can accomplish. Agentic coding, AI assisted development and analysis, and automated workflows can increase human judgment, creativity, and impact rather than replace them. You approach these technologies with curiosity and pragmatism, applying them where they create clear and measurable value.

Above all, leadership is about building people and strengthening the discipline they share. Success is reflected in a team that grows more capable, confident, connected, and effective because of your leadership.

The Essentials

10+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, business intelligence engineering or a related discipline, including 5+ years leading and developing technical teams
Proven track record of building, scaling, and leading high performing teams, turning strong individual contributors into cohesive and highly effective teams that are valued as strategic partners
Depth in building governed, canonical data models and semantic layers, giving core business concepts one authoritative, discoverable definition instead of letting teams reconcile competing sources
Experience designing the data quality, observability, documentation, governance, access control, privacy, lineage, and evaluation systems that ensure data and AI products are reliable, explainable, trustworthy, and safe to operate at scale
Advanced SQL skills and production experience with modern data stack, including AWS, Databricks, Airbyte, Fivetran, Looker, or comparable platforms
Demonstrated ability to lead cross functional data initiatives from strategy through production adoption and measurable business impact
Strong judgment in balancing immediate stakeholder needs with long term investments in reusable data products, platform health, and technical debt reduction
Excellent written and verbal communication with technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior executives

The Nice to Haves

Advanced Python
Experience leading data cleanup efforts and implementing role based access controls and data retention policies to improve data quality, security, and governance
Experience designing and building canonical data models and semantic layers that support financial analysis at scale
Experience leading on call rotations, coordinating incident response, resolving production issues, and driving follow up improvements that strengthen system reliability

At Scribd, Inc., your base pay is one part of your total compensation package and is determined within a range. Our pay ranges are based on the local cost of labor benchmarks for each specific role, level, and geographic location. San Francisco is our highest geographic market in the United States.

In the state of California, the reasonably expected salary range is between $202,500 [minimum salary in our lowest geographic market within California] to $268,000 [maximum salary in our highest geographic market within California].

In the United States, outside of California, the reasonably expected salary range is between $191,500 [minimum salary in our lowest US geographic market outside of California] to $254,000 [maximum salary in our highest US geographic market outside of California].

In Canada, the reasonably expected salary range is between $177,000 CAD[minimum salary in our lowest geographic market] to $235,000 CAD[maximum salary in our highest geographic market].

We carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining compensation, including but not limited to experience; job-related skill sets; relevant education or training; and other business and organizational needs. The salary range listed is for the level at which this job has been scoped. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. This position is also eligible for a competitive equity ownership, and a comprehensive and generous benefits package.

Working at Scribd, Inc.

Are you currently based in a location where Scribd, Inc. can employ you?

Employees must have their primary residence in or near
one of the following cities. This includes surrounding metro areas or locations within a typical commuting distance:

United States

Atlanta | Austin | Boston | Dallas | Denver | Chicago | Houston | Jacksonville | Los Angeles | Miami | New York City | Phoenix | Portland | Sacramento | Salt Lake City | San Diego | San Francisco | Seattle | Washington D.C.

Scribd Flex (flexible work model)
Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage
Mental health support and disability coverage
Generous paid time off, including vacation, sick time, holidays, winter break, volunteer time, and sabbaticals
Paid parental leave and family support benefits
Retirement matching and employee equity
Learning and development programs and professional growth opportunities
Wellness and home office stipends
Complimentary access to the Scribd, Inc. suite of products
Enterprise access to leading AI tools

Get to Know Scribd, Inc.

About Scribd, Inc.

Life at Scribd, Inc.

We want our interview process to be accessible to everyone. You can inform us of any reasonable adjustments we can make to better accommodate your needs by emailing accommodations@scribd.com about the need for adjustments at any point in the interview process.

If you apply for a job with Scribd, Inc. or otherwise engage with us in connection with employment (including as an employee, contractor, or other personnel), the personal information we process in that context is subject to our Employee and Applicant Privacy Policy, which is available here .

Scribd, Inc. is committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We encourage people of all backgrounds to apply, and believe that a diversity of perspectives and experiences create a foundation for the best ideas. Come join us in building something meaningful.

At
Klue
, We’re Building the Future of Competitive Intelligence

We’re looking for a Security, Compliance & IT Leader 👋

As our Director, Enterprise Security & IT
, you'll sit at the intersection of security, compliance, and IT operations. You'll be accountable for how Klue protects customer data and how every Kluebee gets equipped to do their best work. Today, these three areas sit under different teams. You'll turn them into one team with one roadmap, working alongside an Engineering org that already builds and runs our product infrastructure.

Your Mission?
To own the security and compliance posture that our customers, our sales team, and our own people rely on. That covers everything we do: from building the product, to the internal automations, to the tools we use, and how we use AI. You'll set the standard, build the systems and set the rhythm to meet it. And in the process, make the secure way, the easy way.

What's In It for You?

You won't inherit a playbook. You'll write it. You'll define the operating model, the culture, and the technical direction for a brand-new function, and shape a small, sharp team of 2 from day one. You'll report directly to the CTO and work closely with the Senior Leadership Team, as well as the Engineering, Product, Sales, and People teams. You'll tackle big questions like how to govern AI agents connected to company systems, and your answers will set policy at Klue. As Klue grows, so do the team and your scope. You have the power to shape what that looks like.

What You'll Do

Own security posture and incident readiness. Mature how Klue prevents, detects, and responds to security issues. Design the incident response process and governance, and make sure everyone knows their role before something goes wrong.
Run the compliance engine. Own the annual audit cycle against SOC 2 Type II, NIST CSF, and BSIMM, plus penetration testing, from evidence collection to a successful finish. Build audit methodology and documentation that make reviews faster and less painful for the whole company.
Be the security answer for go-to-market. Keep customer questionnaires, external assessments, and audits moving on time. Review and negotiate data protection agreements and security exhibits with customers and vendors so what we sign matches what we do.
Govern vendors, data, and privacy. Run full-spectrum vendor reviews, including sub-processor qualification. Own DLP, data retention, and the privacy framework for an international customer base, including data subject access requests.
Set the rules for AI and high-risk access. Own AI security governance: policies, risk acceptance, data handling, and permissioning for AI tools, agents, and integrations connected to company systems. Define and enforce access governance for high-risk systems, including admin access reviews, service accounts vs. individual credentials, and controls on sensitive logs and data.
Make security engineering's job easier. Set the security and compliance standard for Engineering's security work. Give the team the tooling, policy, and guidelines to build against, and translate their technical work into terms leadership and customers can act on.
Equip and enable every Kluebee. Own devices, access, and tooling across the full employee lifecycle. Manage the vendors behind our IT stack, set and hit reliability targets (SLOs) for corporate systems, and replace ad hoc fixes with repeatable processes that scale. Partner with People so onboarding and offboarding run smoothly. (Product infrastructure stays with Engineering.)

What Success Looks Like

One team, one roadmap. Within two quarters, Security, Compliance, and IT operate as one team with a shared roadmap and a regular operating rhythm.
Customers get fast, consistent answers. Questionnaires, audits, and sub-processor reviews are completed on time and in a repeatable way.
AI and access are governed, not improvised. High-risk systems and AI tools are covered by clear, documented policy, and admin access reviews are routine, not reactive.
Corporate systems are reliable. You define clear SLOs in your first quarter, and Klue meets or beats them.
We're ready when it counts. Incident response governance is documented and understood, and Engineering's security engineers have the tooling and guidelines to respond fast.
Day 1 just works. Every new Kluebee has working equipment and access on their first day, with no scrambling.
The budget is a set of clear choices. You actively manage the function's budget and make defensible tradeoffs between tooling, vendors, and headcount.
You're the default owner. The CTO and SLT turn to you for security, compliance, and IT. Engineering and GTM teams see you as the partner who makes their job easier, not another layer to work around.

What You Bring

Must Haves

You've run security and compliance at a company handling sensitive customer data. You're comfortable owning DLP, data retention, and privacy frameworks, and you can work through a security questionnaire or audit without panic.
You've led IT operations for a whole company, covering equipment, access, and tooling.
You know security frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST) and global privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) in depth.
You're comfortable with ambiguity and building without a playbook.
You communicate clearly with both technical peers and non-technical leaders, and can explain a risk to an engineer and to a CEO.
You've negotiated data protection agreements and security exhibits in vendor and customer contracts.
You understand AI security and governance: data retention commitments, access and permissioning for AI agents and integrations, and risk acceptance for AI tooling.
You've worked closely with product and engineering teams to turn security and compliance goals into reality.

Nice-to-Haves

You've owned a DevOps and/or security engineering function inside a larger engineering org.
You've brought previously siloed security, compliance, and IT teams together under one roof.
You know privacy and data residency frameworks for an international customer base.
You've managed distributed or hybrid teams.

Not ticking every box? That’s okay. We take potential into consideration. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be accepted in lieu of the specifics listed above. If you know you have what it takes, even if that’s different from what we’ve described, be sure to explain why in your application.

If there’s anything we can do to make our hiring process more accessible or to better support you, please let us know, we’re happy to accommodate.

Why Klue Might Be the Perfect Fit For You

At Klue, you’ll push the boundaries of what’s possible. For yourself, your team, and our customers. The environment here feels more startup than corporate. You’ll roll up your sleeves, build, iterate, and level up. This is a place where your ideas matter, you can shape what comes next, and leave your mark.

If you’re looking to join a category-defining company… where you own big outcomes, influence real customers, and work with smart, gritty people… you’ll thrive here.

We love the balance of connection and flexibility. We work Office-First
, with a hybrid touch, and work together in our vibrant offices on Mondays, Wednesdays & Thursdays
to collaborate, brainstorm, and build together.

High Performance Culture. We reward high performance and growth through career development, coaching, and annual performance reviews.

Ownership: All full-time employees have the opportunity to participate in our Employee Stock Option Plan.

Top-tier tools. All employees will receive a Mac (or PC, if that’s your jam) and access to A+ tooling.
AI First. All employees are encouraged to lean into AI to work smarter and faster. Built something cool lately? Show us at our Friday Show, Don’t Tell Meetings.
Growth / Leadership. Direct access to our leadership team, including our CEO, and opportunities to connect with incredible people across the company.
Social connection. There’s no shortage of ways to stay connected and have fun. We get together once a year in Vancouver for a company- wide kickoff. Throughout the year our Hubs hold regular social events.
Dog-friendly spaces. Bring your four-legged friend along in Vancouver or Toronto, as our offices are pup-approved.

About Klue

We’re on a mission to help organizations stop losing winnable deals. Klue’s AI agents generate market, competitor, and buyer insights in a unified platform. We ensure it’s trustworthy, automated, and activated across every department, so they have the answers they need to own their market.

✨ Here’s what makes us tick:

Klue is AI-first at its core. It’s wired deep into our internal processes and tooling, powering our small but mighty team. It drives Klue’s autonomous agents that handle the heavy lifting for customers: collecting intel, generating insights, and ensuring content is updated and available across departments. Our agents help them scale their impact, stay ahead of the market, and reclaim the time that used to be consumed by manual, repetitive busywork.
Competitor Insights. Klue helps revenue teams win more competitive deals by turning market, competitor, and buyer signals into insights teams can actually use. Our AI analyzes calls, CRM data, and real buyer feedback to give product marketers and sellers a clear picture of what’s happening in their market and why deals are won or lost. We’re a curious, collaborative team building a platform that helps companies compete with confidence, and we’re looking for people who want to do meaningful work alongside others who care about craft and impact.
A culture of curiosity, ownership and winning together. We’re a fast-growing, globally-distributed team based in Vancouver (with hubs like Toronto), scaling quicker than ever. We value people who own their domain, act boldly, stay curious and thrive in a collaborative, high-performance environment.
